title: His father's death in Tuscaloosa, 1922
summary: He describes how his father died on July 17, 1922, struck by steel while helping black college students on a barge in Tuscaloosa.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My father died July the 17th, 1922, and he died trying to help some college students to do something that they didn't know how to do. He was on his way to do something else and he said, "I'll show you how to do it," because they were earning their summer money so they could continue their education. And he elected to get up on a barge to try to show them how to do something and the mechanics failed in the machinery and it was like a plow, a piece of steel struck right into his back. When The lathe fell down into these great big wheels and it messed up all the machinery where these cart wheels were going, and he's on top of this barge. Everybody ducked and he ducked, but the piece of steel stuck right in his back, from the back of his neck down to the base of his spine. He was only trying to help about 20 to 30 black college students at that particular time. And It was because of him -
Where was that, Jo? What college was that?

Not the college. I know exactly where it happened. It happened in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, and that's authenticated. It is in the papers; there is a notice to that effect, July the 17th, 1922. I had went there to visit him along with my sister and I was with him on a Sunday and this occurred on a Monday. Monday, July the 17th, 1922, was definitely on a Monday. I can remember that, you see, and everybody from New Orleans on up,

anyone will tell you about my father. That's historical fact, but like I said, we could have been shifted around to Pittsburgh, we could have left Chicago, we could have wherever, and you must remember how the ship-building was, which he was the only one of his kind.
